output.summary: The zero-deviation record is not credible as a quality improvement. Lot rejections rose on all lines (E12), complaints are concentrated on Line 3 lots (E11), and the independent lab and customers disagree with the plant's count. The timing and incentive design (E3) point to suppressed reporting, not training (E2, E7) or tubing (E11). Line 3's output gain matches off-the-books borrowing of technicians from Lines 1 and 4 (E13); output per technician-hour is flat. Line 3's practices are not a transferable model. Suspending the penalty and commissioning an independent investigation with reporter protection are the best next steps. Disciplining the supervisor is premature, and identifying the hotline reporter is harmful. Q1 and Q2 would most sharply test rework and lot traceability.
